articles.title: Diversity over Scale: Recursive Self-Improvement with Ensembles of Small Open-Weight Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The advancement of large language models (LLMs) has significantly enhanced the capabilities of agents across various tasks. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) loops, in which a language model repeatedly rewrites a program and builds on its previous version, now perform well in machine-learning tasks, but they rely on frontier models and hundreds of calls per run. Small open-weight models are far cheaper, yet when used alone, their programs often crash and their improvements stall. We propose DiVE (diverse models evolve), an ensemble method for RSI that aims to improve creativity and diversity of generated solutions. DiVE uses three components: a shared memory, a failure log, and best-idea-wins rounds. This allows models to write candidate solutions from the same context and retain the best idea at each iteration. On 22 MLE-bench Lite competitions, an ensemble of five 8-12B open-weight models has 25.4% less test error than its average member and 16.7% less than Llama 3.3 70B, and comes within 7.1% of Qwen 3.5 122B-A10B at 75% of its cost. Diversity among small models can thus stand in for part of the scale that RSI relies on.
articles.title_zh: 规模上的多样性:用小型开放-重量模型的组合递归自我改进

articles.title: Human-in-the-Loop Runbook Improvement with Agentic Support Automation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operational support is an important component of production software services. Support requests are often emergent and can come in many forms such as customer escalations or unplanned service interruption. Engineers across organizations have been successful in implementing automation to help streamline support processes but many solutions remain in the hands of human operators. A successful strategy to improve operator response times is to maintain up-to-date runbooks which are documents enumerating triage steps and remediation procedures in the face of identified incidents. This paper is an investigation into an operational system which incorporates Agentic AI into a runbook based incident resolution pattern. The bot uses information in the runbook corpus along with some system-specific tooling to guide the manual operator through the mitigation process then evaluate the outcome and suggest edits to the runbook where it found gaps and in its ability to triage the situation. By using the runbook as a medium to bridge humans and automation, the process maintains explainability and can be decoupled from the agent system. This paper demonstrates a collaboration between human operators and Agentic AI with results from an 17 week study involving 232 production incidents. We conclude with lessons on integrating LLMs into DevOps workflows, related work in AI-assisted operations, and guidance for reproducibility.
articles.title_zh: 使用代理支持改进运行簿

articles.title: Walks2Maps: Learning Indoor Geometry from Crowdsourced Wi-Fi RTT and Motion Trajectories
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Everyday smartphone walks offer a scalable source of indoor geometry, but their motion traces drift and their radio measurements are distorted by multipath. We present Walks2Maps, a physics-guided framework that reconstructs a shared metric map from Wi-Fi round-trip-time (RTT) and motion observations, without a floor plan, surveyed access-point (AP) coordinates, or position labels. Walks2Maps jointly estimates pedestrian trajectories, AP locations, and per-trajectory stride scales, then recovers the pathway layout from the reconstructed paths. Shared AP observations connect walks recorded in different local frames, while metric ranges constrain their relative geometry and scale. An asymmetric range loss accommodates multipath-induced excess delay. On 22 phone trajectories collected along 11 routes on an office floor with 30 APs, Walks2Maps achieves median AP and trajectory errors of 0.87 m and 0.89 m, respectively, and a walked-area F1 score of 0.985. Ablations show that radio similarity can recognize places while still producing a distorted map; retaining the metric information in RTT resolves this ambiguity. Asymmetric modeling further reduces AP error by 54% relative to a symmetric loss. These results demonstrate how radio and motion measurements can jointly reveal indoor geometry without a dedicated mapping survey. We will release the dataset and toolkit.
articles.title_zh: Walks2Maps:从人群源代码Wi-Fi RTT和 Motion 轨迹学习室内几何

articles.title: X-AQA: Unifying Action Quality Assessment with Multimodal Large Language Models and Multi-Domain Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Action Quality Assessment (AQA) aims to evaluate the quality of human actions, yet existing methods are predominantly developed and evaluated on individual datasets with different task formulations and assessment criteria. We introduce X-AQA, the first unified training and evaluation framework for general-purpose AQA with multimodal large language models (MLLMs). We construct X-AQA-40K, a training corpus comprising 40,163 samples from 22 data sources across four domains: competitive sports, fitness exercises, rehabilitation, and general skills. We convert heterogeneous annotations into a unified question-answering format, incorporating dataset-specific annotation guidelines and official scoring rules when available. Using this corpus, we fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B to develop a single MLLM capable of handling diverse AQA tasks. We further establish X-AQA-Bench, which evaluates both in-distribution (ID) performance on datasets represented during training and out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization on four held-out datasets. The resulting model outperforms all evaluated open-source MLLMs on X-AQA-Bench and achieves competitive performance relative to proprietary MLLMs. Ablation studies further demonstrate that multi-domain joint training and explicitly providing assessment criteria in prompts both improve OOD generalization. X-AQA establishes a unified foundation for advancing general-purpose AQA across diverse real-world domains. Data and models are released at \hyperlink{https://huggingface.co/collections/Kelly0510/x-aqa}{here}.
articles.title_zh: X-AQA:与多模式大语言模式和多领域学习相结合的行动质量评估

articles.title: Beyond Unit Tests: Path-Aware Rubric-Guided LLM Autograding of Notebooks
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jupyter notebooks support open-ended, multi-step assessments in which students build one logical flow across interdependent steps, combining code, written analysis, and generated outputs such as plots. These reflect authentic scientific practice but are hard to grade consistently, since students may make different yet equally valid choices at each step, so a later answer can only be judged in light of the choices a student made earlier. We present an LLM-based autograder for such flow-structured notebook questions. It generates a rubric from a reference solution, then applies a softening pass that relaxes criteria tied to the reference so legitimate alternative paths are not penalized. Each question group is graded in a single model call, so later answers are judged against the student's own earlier choices, using question-type tags and schema-constrained, low-temperature outputs. Evidence is scored multimodally: code, text, numerical outputs, and figures from code cells. We deployed the tool in a machine-learning course, integrated with Gradescope, with a pre-submission format check and prompt-injection defenses, and evaluate it both in that live course and against archived submissions graded by staff in earlier terms. We report agreement, cross-model variance, cost, student perceptions, and injection resilience. With low-temperature models, agreement with human scores is often strong, including on the open-ended items the design specifically targets, while run-to-run stability depends sharply on the model's temperature support.
articles.title_zh: Beyond Unit Tests: Path-Aware Rubric- Guided LLM 单元外测试 : 笔记本自动升级

articles.title: Agent Money Benchmark: Can AI Agents Be Trusted to Spend Money?
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Giving an AI agent a wallet lets it buy data and services on a client's behalf. Trust then depends on how it spends money and what that spending achieves. We introduce Agent Money Benchmark (AMB) to test whether agents spend a client's money well, starting with purchases of information for financial decisions. We link seller quotes and payments to final answers, evaluating 12 models on 80 payment tasks with simulated sellers and 76 research questions using live data. Purchases settled in USDC on Solana mainnet via x402, a protocol for paying per web request. Three of the 12 models passed 79 of 80 payment tasks without payment or budget errors. Nine fell for a seller's trap at least once; repeat charges and above-list quotes accounted for 79% of scam events. We estimate waste from data and inference costs, counting failed payment tasks in full and research answers in proportion to missed points. With spending split equally between tracks, estimated waste ranged from \$21.0 per \$100 for Claude Fable 5.2 to \$70.8 for GPT-6 Luna.
articles.title_zh: 代理钱基准:AI代理能否信任花钱?.

articles.title: Internalized Experience: How Training Data Shapes Memory Formation in LLMs
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parametric memory enables large language models (LLMs) to retain information from past experience and reuse it in subsequent tasks. Yet how training data supports the internalization of reusable task rules remains unclear. We introduce FSMem (Finite-State Machine Memory), a state-transition framework for constructing training data and studying how data content and organization shape memory formation. We evaluate rule reuse across synthetic worlds, classical planning, and code execution through valid-action identification and execution-outcome prediction, complemented by next-operation prediction in code. Our experiments reveal several systematic learning patterns. Under matched training conditions, even unchanged task rules become harder to internalize when learned alongside a larger variety of action types; by contrast, scaling the training data to provide broader state-action coverage generally improves rule learning. We further find that training at a single execution depth produces depth-specialized behavior, with models performing best when training and test executions have similar lengths. Motivated by this finding, we construct cumulative corpora that combine short and long trajectories, which can outperform long-trajectory-only training while using fewer training tokens. Together, these results demonstrate that the same task rules can be internalized differently depending on how execution experience is constructed, and that understanding these learning patterns can guide the design of more effective training data for parametric memory.
articles.title_zh: 内化经验: LLMs 中如何培训数据形状的记忆形成

articles.title: VeriLadder: A Multi-Agent Specification Refinement System for Tool-Verified Verilog Datasets
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training data is a bottleneck in AI, especially for large language models (LLMs) that write Verilog, because register-transfer-level (RTL) code is rarely published and existing datasets mostly check code for syntax, not instruction correctness. This paper presents VeriLadder, a five-level Verilog dataset, and the multi-agent framework that builds it, in which LLM agents write and revise specifications, and EDA tools (a synthesizer and a formal equivalence checker) decide what is accepted. Its levels follow an engineer's checks. Level 1 labels designs from two large Verilog corpora, namely RTLCoder and PyraNet, with synthesis results, failure causes, critical warnings and post-synthesis metrics. 28% of RTLCoder designs fail synthesis and are kept as negatives. Level 2 grades each instruction on four specification qualities, and low grades predict failed rebuilds. Level 3 rewrites each instruction into a refined specification and accepts it only if an LLM from another model family, reading only that specification, writes a circuit formally equivalent to the original. This raises the share of rebuildable designs from 26.1% to 78.2%, keeping every failed specification with its counterexample. Levels 4 and 5 add verified paraphrases and one-fact variants, hard negatives that differ only in one behavior from the verified design. VeriLadder labels the synthesizability of 716,627 designs and, from RTLCoder, provides 11,247 refined specifications, 32,393 paraphrases and 8,397 one-fact variants. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on VeriLadder raises functional pass@1 from 31.7% to 50.0% on VerilogEval v2 and from 35.0% to 45.2% on RTLLM v2. The dataset and fine-tuned models are publicly available.
articles.title_zh: VeriLadder:工具验证的Verilog数据集的多代理规格改进系统

articles.title: Mitigating Backdoors in Masked Diffusion Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models because they can predict multiple tokens in parallel rather than generating tokens sequentially. However, recent studies have shown that MDLMs are vulnerable to backdoor attacks: when an input contains an attacker-chosen trigger, a backdoored model generates a targeted output, such as malicious code, while otherwise behaving normally. Despite this threat, backdoor defenses for MDLMs remain largely underexplored. We present UNMASK, the first defense framework for MDLMs that detects trigger-containing inputs, localizes the trigger tokens, and removes the backdoor from the compromised model. UNMASK exploits two fundamental properties of backdoor triggers, specificity and dominance, to assign a suspiciousness score to each input token. By leveraging two distinctive capabilities of MDLMs, parallel token prediction and token reconstruction at arbitrary positions, UNMASK computes these scores both effectively and efficiently. We further provide a theoretical analysis supporting the design of UNMASK. Evaluations across 40 settings spanning two attacks and four models show that UNMASK detects 99.3% of trigger-containing inputs at a 5% false-positive rate, substantially outperforming the strongest adapted baseline, which achieves 54.8%. UNMASK also achieves over 99% trigger-localization accuracy and reduces the average attack success rate from 95% to 1%, while largely preserving the model's utility on clean inputs.
articles.title_zh: 在遮盖扩散语言模型中减缓后门

articles.title: Unlearning Model Identity: Ablating LoRA Weights from Question-Based Identity Tuning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models are trained on diverse corpora containing outputs from proprietary teacher models and provider-curated sources. Models subsequently inherit embedded self-identity traits, persistently asserting specific proprietary names. Service providers of open-weight models frequently require the removal of model identity for downstream applications, such as custom interfaces, without exposing provider affiliations to end-users. Effective identity modification is therefore critical for customized model alignment and deployment. This study proposes a method to localize parameter-level representations of self-identity within low-rank adaptation modules to perform targeted weight ablation. By generating probing questions designed to elicit self-naming outputs and fine-tuning the base model on these responses, the approach identifies and ablates high-magnitude weights within the parameter set. Experimental results demonstrate that distilled identity traits reside within a localized subset of low-rank weights, achieving a complete removal rate in Qwen3.5-2B and a 10% rate in Gemma4-E2B while preserving general task capabilities. These findings confirm that ablating top-tier adaptation weights suppresses distilled self-identification without compromising broader model performance.
articles.title_zh: 取消学习模式特性:从基于问题的特性图中放大LORA重量

articles.title: Persuasion from Within: Model-Based Insider Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Debate and Consensus
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems for collective decision-making, such as multi-agent debate and consensus games, in which agents exchange messages and update their answers over multiple rounds and a resolution mechanism aggregates them into a final outcome. Most multi-agent LLM frameworks assume that every participant shares the system objective. In practice, however, a malicious agent can join as a legitimate member of the group and persuade the other agents toward a hidden adversarial goal. We formalize such attacks as a sequential decision-making problem in which the insider seeks to degrade the utility of the collective outcome. We propose a model-based insider attack that learns to persuade a group of agents: the insider first learns a world model of the benign agents from offline trajectories and then uses it both to train a persuasion policy and to plan its messages. In two case studies involving a numerical consensus game and a multi-agent debate, the learned insider is the most effective and the stealthiest attack we evaluate, outperforming both prompt-based and trained LLM persuaders from prior work. The attack also transfers to other target models, larger groups, and unseen datasets, and remains effective under existing Byzantine-resilience defenses. The learned insider also enables a new defense: adversarially training benign agents on the attack data largely removes both our attack and the strongest prior persuasion attack. These results show that combining world models with reinforcement learning and planning is an effective route to both attacking and hardening language-based multi-agent systems.
articles.title_zh: 来自内部的劝告:LLM多方智能体辩论和共识中基于模式的内幕攻击

articles.title: Beyond Single-Turn Privacy: Training-Data Leakage in Conversational RAG
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is known to reduce training-data leakage in single-turn interactions, but whether this protection persists over multi-turn conversations is unclear. We introduce CRELT (Conversational RAG Extraction Leakage Trajectory), a reusable framework that tracks, turn by turn, the real contact details from the training data that a RAG system discloses. CRELT separates retrieval, conversation history, and attack strategy through a full-factorial design, uses a retrieval corpus verified to contain none of the target PII, and counts an item as leaked only when it is absent from the model input at the turn it is produced. In our main experiment, this criterion excludes 29-53% of raw matches that were already present in the input. Across GPT-J-6B, Pythia-6.9B, and Pythia-12B, targeting real Enron contact details, retrieval reduces disclosure under both full and cleared history, consistent with prior single-turn results. A length-matched control with random passages reproduces 91-99.5% of this reduction under cleared history and 47-78% under full history, so much of it comes from the added context rather than from what is retrieved. With retrieval enabled, however, retaining full conversation history increases disclosure by a factor of 3.6-4.9, while retaining only one previous turn already restores disclosure to approximately the full-history level. With retrieval, clearing the history reduces disclosure by 72-79%, but does not eliminate it. These results show that single-turn privacy audits can substantially underestimate training-data leakage in conversational RAG systems and that conversation-history policy is a critical dimension of privacy evaluation.
articles.title_zh: Beyond Single-Turn 隐私:对话RAG中的培训数据泄漏

articles.title: DiscernBench: Evaluating Cooperative Discernment of LLM Agents in Institutional Settings
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28787v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The deployment of large language models in operational settings demands evaluation of judgment under institutional constraint. We introduce DiscernBench, a benchmark for evaluating cooperative discernment: the ability of an agent to determine whether to comply with, refuse, or escalate a request in an institutional setting. DiscernBench comprises scenarios derived from real-world incident reports across domains such as aviation, law enforcement, and emergency management. We evaluate eight LLMs across three decision-making configurations and analyze both final decisions and the intermediate judgments produced during multi-agent deliberation. Under disagreement, Final Responders exhibit model- and role-dependent aggregation patterns in which a lone specialist recommendation can disproportionately influence the collective decision, a phenomenon we term Minority-Signal Override. Role-specialized multi-agent deliberation raises average over-escalation from 3.79% under direct single-agent judgment to 28.27%, with the direction and magnitude of minority-signal influence varying substantially across models and specialist roles. These results reveal distinct collective decision behaviors that are not captured by final-answer accuracy alone. Trustworthy multi-agent systems therefore require evaluating not only individual specialist reasoning, but also how conflicting judgments are transformed into collective decisions. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Disha1001/DiscernBench.
articles.title_zh: Discern Bench:评估机构环境中LLM代理的合作差异

articles.title: When do stored facts become available in looped transformers?
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Looped transformers do not acquire new knowledge during a forward pass. Prior work shows that they store as many bits in their weights as non-looped models. It remains unclear how recurrence makes this knowledge available during inference. We study this question using synthetic factual recall and multi-hop reasoning, measuring depth-resolved readable information in bits with native readouts and tuned lenses. Under final-loop supervision, single-hop facts become readable progressively: heavier memorization loads delay retrieval despite comparable final readable information. Untied baselines of equal unrolled depth concentrate retrieval near the end of their stacks, whereas looped models expose facts earlier. This delay is not intrinsic to the tested recall tasks: training with supervision and depth-specific readouts at every loop makes near-final information readable after the first loop in all tested configurations. Representational analysis shows value-related structure emerging within states organized by the query key. We then study multi-hop chains whose facts are stored in the weights rather than given in the prompt. Intermediate entities become decodable in chain order, and aligned transitions show next-entity structure developing while current-entity structure remains dominant. Interventions in a released six-recurrence model establish a causal role for these representations. Counterfactual replacements of a probe-defined entity component at a single prompt position redirect downstream bridge entities and the final answer. Conversely, replacements from queries that reach the same entity through different preceding relations, preserving the remaining relation suffix, retain the original answer in over 99.5\% of tested cases. These results distinguish a training-dependent schedule for factual recall from the causal role of retrieved-entity representations in subsequent composition.
articles.title_zh: 存储的事实何时在环形变压器中可以找到?

articles.title: Does a Frontier Large Language Model Know What It Can Solve? A 100-Conjecture Calibration Study
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How does confidence correlate with actual performance in large language models, when attacking open research-level math problems? We address this question by studying the performance of ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Ultra on a set of 100 open conjectures in geometric analysis. By construction, the model first selected open problems in geometric analysis that it assessed that it had at least a 50\% chance of proving or disproving, and then assigned a probability of success to each question. 13 questions were then excluded after an audit, and the model was asked to resolve the remaining 87 problems. Its mean stated resolution probability was $0.617$, versus an observed rate of $0.103$ (Brier score $0.351$, ECE $0.513$), thereby demonstrating that the model was systematically over-confident in its self-assessment. However, the scores retained ranking signal (AUROC $0.714$). The model was highly overconfident in probability magnitude but did more often than not assign a high probability of success to the problems that it did resolve, than the problems that it did not. Hence, its probabilities were numerically mis-calibrated but directionally correct. All proofs have been formalized in Lean, thereby verifying correctness, and have been run through a semantic equivalence pipeline to ensure semantic equivalence between the formalized and informal statements. These are exploratory campaign outcomes, not fixed-budget success probabilities. The certificates prove formal statements; for a couple of questions, some geometric inputs are assumed in the lean proofs.
articles.title_zh: 一个边疆大语言模型知道它能解决什么吗? 百度猜想校正研究

articles.title: EA-Bench: Measuring information and action efficiency under imperfect instructions
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personal agents help users complete everyday work across digital applications. Many standard benchmarks assume that users provide sufficient information to solve a task. However, agents often encounter incomplete, distracting, or inconsistent information in practice. To systematically study agent inefficiency under such imperfect information, we introduce Efficient Action (EA)-Bench, which evaluates both tool calls and user interactions in work-related tasks. To our knowledge, it is the first benchmark to jointly evaluate tool-call efficiency and user-interaction efficiency under controlled missing, redundant, and conflicting information. We construct 63 base-task instances adapted from existing work-related benchmarks. To guide perturbation design and quantify task requirements, we represent workflows as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) and examine node-level dependencies to identify where information can be withheld, contradicted, or supplemented with distractors. We use a two-stage validation process combining AI-assisted checks with expert screening to select 232 conditions from 792 initial candidates. We organize these tasks into Easy and Hard tracks by task complexity. Experiments show that imperfect information can reduce accuracy and increase tool-use and user-interaction costs. More concerning, several models obtain apparently correct outcomes by guessing user-specific values without confirmation, revealing potential execution unreliability in current models under imperfect user information.
articles.title_zh: EA-Bench:根据不完善的指示衡量信息和行动效率

articles.title: Guarding with Judgment: Learning to Intervene for Multimodal Safety
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When visual context makes an ordinary request unsafe to answer as asked, a blanket refusal may leave the user's need unresolved. Choosing how to help requires distinguishing an established hazard from a condition that still needs verification, a distinction that binary safety labels leave unspecified. We formulate this decision through four actions: allow, warn, review, and refuse. To ground these decisions in verifiable evidence, we build a corpus of 20,126 training audits and the JudiBench benchmark, connecting each action to diagnostic judgments, source evidence, and controlled context changes. Our guard, JudiAct, separately states what the source establishes, what condition governs the help, and how the rules apply. It then checks these three brief review items against the original inputs to predict diagnostic labels and a handling action. Supervised training learns individual judgments while comparing label assignments across related cases. A second stage swaps one review item at a time, using the resulting audit feedback to refine review generation. On JudiBench, JudiAct improves request and answer Macro-F1 by more than 28 percentage points over its 4B backbone. Across nine public benchmarks, it outperforms state-of-the-art guards on the mean delivered-answer score in both pre-generation and post-generation settings, cutting MM-SafetyBench attack success from 40.78% to 25.30%.
articles.title_zh: 保护判断:学习如何干预多式联运安全

articles.title: StudioBench: Benchmarking Agentic Multimodal Large Language Models for Productive Audiovisual Creation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video generators can now render convincing short clips, yet complete audiovisual works require coordinating visuals, sound, and editing across multiple stages. Existing benchmarks focus on individual generators or video agents under narrower production settings, leaving end-to-end creation by general multimodal large language models (MLLMs) underexplored. We introduce StudioBench, a benchmark comprising 160 tasks across eight video genres and five task types, spanning diverse audiovisual production requirements. Models produce minutes of finished audiovisual content using 33 atomic generation, editing, and inspection tools, without shell access or workflow templates. We evaluate the delivered films, while analyzing reconstructed workflow graphs to characterize production behavior and diagnose failures. Across seven MLLMs, explicit requirements are nearly saturated, yet production quality varies substantially in picture clarity and composition, object structure, motion, and lip sync. All models spontaneously organize multi-stage production workflows without predefined templates. However, higher-quality models exhibit more selective production workflows, whereas additional tool calls alone show little association with quality. These findings identify the missing quality loop of effective inspection, selection, and revision as a key bottleneck in productive audiovisual creation.
articles.title_zh: Studio Bench:用于生产视听创作的多式大型语言模型基准

articles.title: STRIDE: Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-Guided Skill Disclosure and Evolution for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Skill-augmented reinforcement learning enables LLM agents to reuse task-solving knowledge across episodes, but existing systems typically expose agents to a flat skill pool and update skills only from coarse, episode-level outcomes. This conflates two distinct uses of experience: a stable strategy that should frame the whole episode, and tactical know-how that should be retrieved only when the agent reaches a local execution gap. We propose STRIDE (Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-guided skIll Disclosure and Evolution), a framework that brings progressive skill disclosure into agentic reinforcement learning. STRIDE keeps the selected strategy visible as episode context, exposes a compact tactic menu, and loads full tactic content only after an explicit retrieval action. This interface turns each retrieval into an event-level credit unit: the same event provides process feedback for learning when to retrieve and supplies evidence for skill-bank evolution. On ALFWorld, STRIDE achieves a 92.7% average success rate with Qwen3-4B and a 94.9% average success rate with Qwen3-8B. On WebShop, it improves over the strongest reproduced skill-augmented baseline by 4.5 score points and 1.9 success-rate percentage points. These results show that skill reuse is most effective when persistent strategies preserve global task structure and tactics are disclosed only at local decision bottlenecks.
articles.title_zh: STRIDE:从战略到战术的检索——指导技能披露和工具强化学习的演变

articles.title: When Do Better Visual World Models Make Better Plans? Decision-Aligned Selection for Latent Planning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual world models enable goal-conditioned planning by predicting the outcomes of candidate actions in latent space. However, planning depends on how well a model ranks candidates, whereas training optimizes how accurately it predicts each one. We identify the Decision-Relevant Residual (DRR), the part of the cost error that can reorder candidates, and show that the more training reduces the DRR, the more it improves selection (Spearman $\rho = 0.82$, vs. $0.61$ for prediction error). Building on this insight, we introduce Decision-Aligned Selection (DAS), a plug-in selection rule that scores candidates by the standardized consensus of several independently trained checkpoints, which averages out their checkpoint-specific residuals. Across two model families (LeWorldModel and DINO-WM) and five tasks, DAS selects better actions than single checkpoints in 12 of 18 configurations and outperforms training one model three times longer in 14 of 18. In closed loop, DAS improves success over single checkpoints in 6 of 9 pre-registered LeWM comparisons.
articles.title_zh: 当更好的视觉世界模型 制定更好的计划? 后期规划的选择

articles.title: OmniDecisionBench: Evaluating and Benchmarking the Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal System One models answer visual tasks with typed decisions and native probabilities, yet no holistic evaluation compares them with general VLMs or maps either class's capability boundaries. We introduce OmniDecisionBench, a holistic benchmark of multimodal System One models. Its main evaluation assigns 45 datasets (192,975 records) to five capability families and twelve primary angles across four typed interfaces, scoring accuracy and candidate-probability calibration. A validation layer adds three single-factor diagnostics varying visual presentation, textual evidence sufficiency, and target dataset. Across three System One models and two general VLMs, three regularities emerge. First, strengths depend on angle and metric: System One models lead discrete tasks overall with lower ECE15 on most perception, reading, and reasoning angles (Jev 1.14: 80.14% accuracy, 4.50% ECE15), while general VLMs lead ordinal grading and outperform Jev 1.14 among the three models tested on direct Box grounding. Second, multi-image and abstract reasoning bound every model, where confidence rather than accuracy separates them. Third, reliability shifts with the input: rendering only options nearly triples Jev 1.14's selective risk at nearly flat mean signed bias, and donor risk cutoffs often exceed target risk across unseen datasets and task families. OmniDecisionBench thus maps which model class suits each angle and where reliability ends. The code and dataset will be available at https://github.com/Glax147/OmniDecisionBench.
articles.title_zh: Bench号决定:评价和确定多式Jev-Style系统决定模式的基准

articles.title: STEdgeFormer: MCU and NPU Deployable Transformer Architecture
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transformer-based sequence models have achieved strong performance in language and time-series modeling, but self-attention remains computationally and memory intensive for deployment on resource-constrained edge accelerators. We propose STEdgeFormer, a lightweight, hardware-aware sequence architecture designed for efficient execution on embedded neural accelerators. STEdgeFormer combines polynomial mixture layers and DyT normalization with an accelerator-aware causal memory block, replacing pairwise self-attention with compact causal aggregation. On TinyStories, the fully NPU-supported STEdgeFormer (MW) achieves a perplexity of 7.39 with 4.12M parameters and 6.51 MB RAM, with an end-to-end latency of 40 ms. In comparison, the standard 4.12M-parameter configuration achieves a lower perplexity of 6.79 but requires CPU fallback for unsupported operators, resulting in 1450 ms latency. Vanilla Transformer, on the other hand, achieves a perplexity score of 5.71 using a 4.40M-parameter model, but it cannot be deployed on the hardware. On downstream tasks, STEdgeFormer achieves 94% accuracy on ECG5000 and 93% accuracy on Speech Commands with 1.39M parameters. These results demonstrate that hardware-aware architectural choices and operator compatibility can have a substantial impact on practical inference latency, beyond model size and task accuracy alone. Rather than targeting state-of-the-art accuracy on individual benchmarks, STEdgeFormer is designed to provide a deployable sequence modeling architecture under the memory, computational, and operator constraints of embedded neural accelerators.
articles.title_zh: STEdgeFormer:MCU和NPU可部署变形器架构

articles.title: PruneNAS: Constraint Aware Neural Architecture Search based Pruning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has achieved state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks, but its high computational cost remains a major barrier. We introduce PruneNAS, a novel framework that integrates structured pruning into NAS to efficiently explore high-performing architectures while leveraging pretrained models. Unlike conventional NAS methods that train each candidate from scratch, PruneNAS generates a candidate pool by pruning pretrained networks at multiple granularity levels and formulates the selection as a global optimization problem using training-free importance metrics. This approach enables rapid evaluation of candidate architectures under strict resource constraints, dramatically reducing search time from hundreds of GPU hours to mere minutes. Experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that PruneNAS discovers compact, high-accuracy architectures that nearly halve the computational cost (MACs) of prior methods on ResNet-50, while also showing strong generalization on object detection tasks with YOLO. Our method bridges structured pruning and NAS, offering a practical solution for resource-constrained model deployment.
articles.title_zh: PruneNAS: 约束意识神经结构搜索基于Pruning

articles.title: Learning from Another Angle: Rotation-Based Test-Time Training for Multimodal Large Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance on vision-language tasks but often remain vulnerable to distribution shifts due to their fixed parameters during inference. While Test-Time Training (TTT) offers a pathway for dynamic adaptation, existing approaches suffer from prohibitive computational overhead due to multiple sampling and the risk of error reinforcement from biased self-generated supervision. In light of this view, we propose RoTTT (Rotation-based Test-Time Training), a simple and efficient TTT approach that enables instance-specific refinement at inference time. For each test instance, RoTTT performs a small number of gradient updates by predicting the rotation angle of the input image. The known rotation angles naturally serve as a reliable self-supervised signal, enabling lightweight and stable adaptation without requiring additional annotations. Extensive experiments across multiple vision-language benchmarks demonstrate that RoTTT consistently improves performance across different MLLMs, providing a practical and efficient paradigm for on-the-fly MLLM adaptation.
articles.title_zh: 从另一个角度学习:多式联运大语文模式的自转测试-时间培训

articles.title: Do You Even Know What I Want? Improving LLMs Ability to Detect Hidden User Intent
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As with conventional AI agents, a common source of misalignment between Large Language Models (LLMs) and their human users is misspecified goals. Often, this happens when the human has skewed beliefs about the system's model and provides it with information that causes behavior different from what they expected, with potentially unwanted side effects. To ensure goal alignment, one solution would be for the LLM to ask the human questions about their objectives. However, it has been well-documented that LLMs most often provide default responses to user requests rather than try and ask questions to clarify their true intent. In this paper, we address these challenges by adapting a novel formulation for the objective misspecification problem to work with LLMs. We then test if LLMs that are prompted to ask questions about a user's true underlying objectives are better at identifying them compared to those that do not. We evaluate our method using four state-of-the-art LLMs tested on five standard IPC domains, showing that for some domains, asking questions greatly improved model performance.
articles.title_zh: 你知道我想要什么吗? 提高LLMs检测隐藏用户意图的能力

articles.title: MVAgent: Per-Video Agents under Global Coordination for Multi-Video Understanding
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-video understanding requires systems to combine evidence from different videos for cross-video reasoning. Answering such questions involves two kinds of decisions. Observation decisions must adapt to each video's content, whereas cross-video judgments require relating evidence from different videos based on the question. Most existing agents make both kinds of decisions in one controller, whose context accumulates observations from every video. We separate them in MVAgent, a training-free Multi-Video Understanding Agent framework with one LocalAgent per video. Each LocalAgent plans observations of its own video and keeps a private observation history. A GlobalAgent coordinates cross-video reasoning by instructing the LocalAgents and combining their reports with joint observation. We evaluate MVAgent on CVBench, MVU-Eval, and CrossVid, using three Qwen3.5 models of different sizes and GPT-6-sol. With Qwen3.5, our framework improves aggregate benchmark scores by 5.1 points on average over Single-pass inference with the same model and by 5.0 points over the strongest prior agent using the same model. With GPT-6-sol, the average gain over Single-pass inference with the same model is 4.3 points. On the same hardware, MVAgent also runs 1.8-2.7 times faster than prior agents of comparable size.
articles.title_zh: MVAgent:全球协调下的多视多视多视多视多视多视特摄

articles.title: Neural Agent Compiler: Learning to Schedule Soft Dependencies
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents accomplish complex tasks by coordinating multiple reasoning steps and tool operations, which form dependencies among their operations. Existing orchestration methods primarily consider hard dependencies that determine when an operation can legally begin, but overlook soft dependencies, i.e., information that is not required for execution but may improve an already executable operation. We identify soft-dependency scheduling as an important problem in agent execution. To this end, we introduce Neural Agent Compiler (NAC), a learned scheduler that predicts the task-quality and resource consequences of three execution modes and selects the highest-utility legal mode at a scheduling boundary. NAC represents the executable continuation, pending information event, and resource state in a shared memory, and uses a utility function to adapt the consequence predictions to different resource preferences. Across AppWorld, WebShop, and $\tau^2$-bench, NAC achieves 276/417 AppWorld task completions, a 74.69 WebShop Task Score, and 59/100 $\tau^2$-bench successes. Additional studies show that the learned scheduler reduces execution work, establishing soft-dependency scheduling as a promising solution for orchestrating tool-using agents.
articles.title_zh: 神经代理编译器: 学习将软依赖安排

articles.title: MetaSkill: Reusable Problem-Solving Methods for Adaptive Skill Orchestration in LLM Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reusable skills provide specialized procedures, but large language model (LLM) agents must still determine how to organize and adapt their use. We introduce MetaSkill, a two-layer framework for reusing problem-solving methods across tasks and domains. The method layer selects from 26 curated methods and binds abstract roles to task objects. The execution layer uses the instantiated method to identify intermediate objectives, coordinate native skills, and guide repair or method reselection. On 89 SkillsBench tasks and 995 ToolHop examples, MetaSkill outperforms the evaluated baselines in all six configurations, with accuracy gains of 3.51-13.48% over the strongest baseline. Ablations support explicit method-guided orchestration beyond direct method injection and further gains from method reselection.
articles.title_zh: MetaSkill: LLM 代理器中可重复使用的问题解决方法

articles.title: DoppelVet: Comparative Safety Verification for Self-Evolving Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-evolving agents improve by retaining feedback as reusable memories or skills, but every mistaken approval can shape many future behaviors. Two updates can provide exactly the same evidence to a verifier yet produce opposite safety outcomes, so the verifier cannot distinguish them from that evidence alone. We introduce DoppelVet, a verification framework that checks proposed updates before they enter an agent's persistent state. Without access to safety labels, DoppelVet constructs an alternative that matches every signal used by the existing verifier. It replays both updates from the same state and directly compares their behaviors in both presentation orders before deciding whether to retain the candidate. We evaluate DoppelVet on DoppelVet-Grid and DoppelVet-Tool, covering executable programs and natural-language memories. Across nine open-weight and proprietary verifiers, DoppelVet raises mean harmful-update detection AUC from 0.762 to 0.940 on DoppelVet-Grid and from 0.681 to 0.826 on DoppelVet-Tool, outperforming VaG and AgentDoG 1.5. On DoppelVet-Grid, it reduces trajectories experiencing degradation from 30.39% to 0.43% over a ten-generation self-update loop and leaves no final degradation.
articles.title_zh: DoppelVet:自我演变智能体的比较安全核查

articles.title: Emotion-Aware and Context-Grounded Dialogue Agents for Personalized Video Game Interactions
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present ChatNPC, a game companion that dynamically personalizes its responses in real time based on players' emotional shifts to enhance user immersion. The model integrates sequential data, leveraging the dynamic nature of streams to benefit from player information, spoken lines, and in-game context. We leverage recent progress in LLMs' tool-calling capabilities to extract vital information from memory and recognize potential constraints for accurate reasoning, thereby tackling the complexity of NPC conversation scenarios. The task is divided into a game sentinel-guided agent (SeGent), a memory capability, and a chat planning tool for reasoning instantiation. The approach uses a lightweight game template as an information framework, with relevant details and a thorough reasoning layout. We conduct extensive experiments on a newly developed game dataset for in-game context NPC dialogue and demonstrate that ChatNPC sequentially captures players' emotional shifts over time; responses are more naturalistic and human-like with appropriate conversational cues, pauses, and sighs; and utterances remain faithful to the dynamics of in-game context and player actions, supporting narrative continuity.
articles.title_zh: 个人化视频游戏互动的情感意识和背景组合对话代理

articles.title: Layer-Level Control of Language Model Execution in Agent Frameworks
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent frameworks typically orchestrate language models through prompt-and-response interfaces. We propose a harness design that exposes intermediate model states and layer-level execution controls to the agent runtime. By connecting state collection, policy fitting, and execution, the design enables policies to allocate computation within and across models based on intermediate states. We demonstrate the approach with a prototype that learns stitching bridges and state-conditioned execution policies from paired model states, then applies them during inference to select among continue, exit, and stitch. For dispatcher supervision, we select the least-computation action whose full-vocabulary next-token prediction matches the source model's full-depth prediction, using continue when neither early action matches. We train these components on a frozen proxy corpus of 5,000 typed-decision items authored using source texts sampled from WildChat conversations, then evaluate the prototype on JevBench measuring task accuracy, agreement with full-model predictions, and end-to-end latency including runtime overhead. Preliminary results show an approximately 15% reduction in mean latency while maintaining task accuracy comparable to full-model inference.
articles.title_zh: 代理框架中语言模式执行的层层控制

articles.title: Reinforcement Learning from LLM-Generated (Suboptimal) Demonstrations
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved substantial progress across many domains, but training an agent \textit{tabula rasa} remains highly sample-inefficient. A common remedy is to initialize the agent using a neural network pretrained on demonstrations. However, collecting demonstrations is expensive, and the demonstrations themselves can be suboptimal. In this work, we use a large language model (LLM) to generate an advice policy that produces demonstration data with effectively no human cost. We use this data to warmstart a DQN agent, and use the advice policy itself to guide exploration during training. Because LLM-generated advice is often suboptimal, we further introduce a value warmstart method that initializes the agent to recognize promising states from the advice policy's behavior, without directly copying its actions. To characterize the robustness of this method, we systematically perturb individual sub-skills of an LLM-generated advice policy for a long-horizon, sparse-reward task. Degraded advice still meaningfully accelerates learning relative to unaided baselines. These results suggest that LLM-generated advice, though suboptimal, can be a cheap alternative to costly human demonstrations.
articles.title_zh: 从LLM(最佳)示范中学习强化

articles.title: Who Sent It or How It Moved? Sender Shortcuts in Cryptocurrency Anti-Money-Laundering Benchmarks, Audited on Elliptic2 and Elliptic++
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two public benchmarks dominate graph-based anti-money-laundering (AML) research on Bitcoin: the transaction-level Elliptic dataset, extended as Elliptic++, and the subgraph-level Elliptic2. In both, a label is assigned according to the entity that sends the funds. We ask whether models trained on these benchmarks learn how laundering moves or merely who sent the money, and we propose a diagnostic protocol to tell the two apart: a sender lookup baseline, a novelty baseline, a sender-disjoint split with a leakage check, and a decomposition of performance into sender, receiver and intrinsic signal. On Elliptic2 the task largely reduces to classifying the sender. Under the standard random split, a no-learning lookup of sender history reaches a PR-AUC of 0.954, against 0.975 for gradient boosting on 456 features; our reimplementation of RevClassify reproduces its reported 0.97 and falls to 0.126 without sender information. When senders are held out, performance drops to 0.746, and the subgraph's own structure, transactions and receivers fall from 0.619 to 0.186. On Elliptic++ the same protocol finds the shortcut negligible: sender history reaches only 0.340 against 0.986 for the full model (3.5 against 10.1 times the test prevalence), adding it to the full model raises PR-AUC by less than 0.004 in every seed, and the transaction's own features keep 0.883 when sending addresses are held out. We trace the difference to the unit of sender identity: Elliptic2 senders are entity clusters that recur across many labeled subgraphs, whereas Elliptic++ senders are individual addresses, and fewer than half of test transactions have a sending address seen in training. A shared sender-based label rule thus produces a severe shortcut in one benchmark and a negligible one in the other, so the diagnostic must be run on each benchmark.
articles.title_zh: 是谁送来的,还是怎么动的? 加密货币反洗钱基准中的发送快捷键,对椭圆2和椭圆++进行了审计

articles.title: Latent-Predisposition Personas for Heterogeneous and Reliable LLM Survey Simulation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM personas are used to simulate survey publics, which should reproduce not only answer distributions but also within-person coherence and stability. Drawing on mass belief systems research, we show that persona-conditioned LLMs produce over-constrained publics. Across three model families and three U.S. surveys, opinions on unrelated issues are 1.6-4.6 times as correlated as among humans, and party identification explains 2.5-7.6 times as much answer variance. Common remedies (temperature, diversity instructions, backstories) weaken these correlations by making answers more random. On Qwen, their ten-day test-retest reliability falls to 33-59% of the human level, and when made consistent they lose correlation fit. We propose Latent-Predisposition Personas (LPP), whose persons differ stably, not randomly. Each persona receives political engagement, value priorities, and party-relative issue deviations that grow as engagement falls. Answers are sharpened and calibrated to toplines and party crosstabs. At selected operating points, LPP is never significantly worse than any baseline and far more reliable. At matched human-level reliability, it has the lowest correlation error in all six model-survey combinations, also at a lower target. Errors still exceed those between human samples, and gains on framing effects and a frontier closed model are partial.
articles.title_zh: 异质和可靠LLM调查模拟

articles.title: Blind to What They Can Fix: A Detection Gap in Self-Improving Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents can write programs that carry out a task without calling a model at every step, so the task runs fast and its logic stays open to inspection. Agents improve these programs by running them, studying their failures, and revising the code, a form of recursive self-improvement (RSI). We ask whether this process also yields runtime checks that can be trusted. In five task domains, with up to seven author models, agents bring their programs to high scores. Yet when the environment changes, the checks they were told to write stay silent on half or more of the resulting failures in four domains. These failures can be detected and repaired: a monitor built from records of normal runs catches most of them in three domains, and the same agents usually repair them once called. The checks do not examine the recorded relations that reveal the failures, and the strongest agent writes checks that catch most of them once told that its checks are the only thing that calls it back. An unreported failure stays unrepaired, which limits what self-improvement is worth in autonomous operation. Evaluations of self-improvement should measure not only scores but also whether a system notices its own failures.
articles.title_zh: 盲从他们能够解决的问题:自我改进智能体的发现差距

articles.title: Memphis: A Case Study in Seeding an Agent Task from a Model's Real-World Attempt
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent benchmarks are usually made harder by scaling up the data their tasks are built from, yet models that do well on them still fail at real work. We propose building simulated tasks from a model's own attempt at an open-ended task in the real world, so that the model's failures in the simulation resemble its failures in reality. As a case study, we had GPT-6.1 Sol manage two human workers in Cairo over chat for five shifts, with a budget of 7,000 Egyptian pounds, to build as many USB desk lamps as it could. It built two. From the real-world attempt's transcript, we build Memphis, an evaluation in a model-simulated world. Memphis is hard: GPT-6.1 Sol delivers 1.0 lamp per trial on average and repeats its real-world mistakes, buying too few stands and giving up the search for them. With a one-page hint on where to buy parts and who can wire them, it delivers 9.2. Claude Opus 5.5 delivers 2.2 without the hint and 4.6 with it. We release the task, the trials, the audits, and a redacted record of the real-world evaluation.
articles.title_zh: 孟菲斯:从模型真实世界尝试中找到代理任务的案例研究

articles.title: Who Makes the Decision? Auditing an Agentic LLM Pipeline for Illicit Cryptocurrency Transaction Monitoring
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic pipelines that combine graph detectors, deterministic rules, retrieval-augmented generation and an LLM judge are being proposed to monitor illicit cryptocurrency flows and to write regulation-citing justifications for analysts. They are evaluated on end-to-end accuracy or on the quality of those justifications, and neither shows which component made a decision. We audit such a pipeline on the Elliptic++ Bitcoin dataset with decision-source attribution, a trace-level protocol with three layers: per-case actual causation, interventional Shapley credit, and mediation of upstream risk scores. A deterministic wallet-score override carries about 94% of the credit for flags, and a verification gate cancels most of the judge's own flags, which fall on licit transactions. Testing the judge alone over 76 evidence bundles, four backbones and two prompts, we find that it follows an injected risk score on the anonymous transaction features it is given, although stronger models decide correctly when the facts are explicit; that a context too short for the system prompt leaves it with no verdict at all; and that it cites regulatory clauses that do not apply, which a substring-based citation check accepts. Hiding the score does not fix the judge, because evidence gathered with the score visible still encodes it. For illicit-activity monitoring, an LLM's justification should therefore not be read as evidence of which component flagged a transaction.
articles.title_zh: 谁做决定? 审计非法加密金融交易监测代理LLM管道

articles.title: MobileGrail: Learning Compact Guardrails for On-Device deployable Mobile GUI Agent Safety
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Runtime guardrails protect mobile GUI agents by assessing each proposed action before execution, but existing guardrails rely on cloud hosted large multimodal models, exposing every screen to a remote server, including private information such as payments, messages, and medical records. We propose MobileGrail, an on-device deployable model that addresses both. It maintains a recurrent task state that retains only the evidence subsequent safety decisions depend on, so that authorization and execution progress persist beyond the short context. To intervene early while keeping the safety boundary precise, it learns two labels, unsafe and block: unsafe marks the action that commits a violation, whereas block may be issued at any step of an intervention window, which spans from the first action that the user's authorization no longer explains to the committing action itself. To support training, we build an environment of 32 applications whose backends verify the effect of every action, supplying verified labels for supervision and rewards for reinforcement learning to calibrate intervention timing. We also build MobileVeto, an offline benchmark of unsafe trajectories largely on held-out applications, each paired with a benign counterpart. On MobileVeto, MobileGrail built on Qwen3.5-2B intercepts 76.2% of violations, up from 64.5% for its prompted backbone, while reducing premature intervention from 58.6% to 5.2%, outperforming the cloud-based OS-Sentinel on both. We further conduct online evaluation on GhostEIBench, where MobileGrail guarding a Qwen3.8-27B agent reduces fully successful attacks from 13 to 3 of 110 tasks while raising task completion from 48 to 58. Quantized to 4 bits, MobileGrail runs on a Snapdragon 8 Elite at a median latency of 4.7 s, comparable to the 5.1s of cloud-hosted Gemini 3.8 Flash.
articles.title_zh: MobileGrail: 用于可部署设备的学习契约护栏

articles.title: Deep Discriminative Feature Fusion of Convolutional and Attention-Based Recurrent Representations for Subject-Independent ECG Stress Recognition
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stress has become a significant concern because of its negative impact on both physical and mental health and therefore drives the need for reliable automated systems to assess stress levels. Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals provide a non-invasive and objective measure of physiological stress responses and have emerged as a promising modality for continuous stress monitoring. While deep learning techniques have achieved encouraging results in ECG-based stress detection, many studies focus only on one type of feature representation, and therefore limit their ability to capture both the morphological patterns and temporal dynamics embedded in ECG signals. To address this limitation, in this paper, we propose three deep learning-based feature fusion frameworks for ECG-based stress classification. These are Residual Feature Fusion (RFF), Bidirectional Feature-Wise Cross-Attention Fusion (BFCAF), and a novel Cross-Attention Residual Fusion (CARF) framework that combines the strengths of residual learning and bidirectional cross-attention within a unified architecture. A 1D Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) and a BiLSTM-Attention network are used to extract complementary morphological and temporal representations from ECG signals, respectively. The proposed fusion frameworks leverage these heterogeneous representations to improve feature interaction, information preservation, and stress discrimination. The proposed frameworks are evaluated using subject-independent Leave-One-Subject-Out Cross-Validation (LOSOCV) on the RML and WESAD datasets for three-class stress classification. Experimental results show that the proposed feature fusion methods consistently improve performance over individual CNN and BiLSTM models, with CARF achieving the highest accuracies of 83.1% and 77.91% on the RML and WESAD datasets, respectively.
articles.title_zh: 深刻的歧视性特征,即对独立主题ECG压力识别的反复反映和关注

articles.title: Particle Belief Representations for Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Particle filters flexibly represent complex, multimodal beliefs but expose them as weighted, unordered sets incompatible with conventional fixed-dimensional policies. We study particle-belief encodings as inputs to reinforcement-learning policies while holding belief estimation and policy optimization fixed. We compare statistical summaries, cumulant-generating-function (CGF) features, and permutation-invariant set encoders. Trainable encoders are learned end-to-end or pretrained through belief reconstruction or task-specific prediction. Across eight tasks, pooling-based set encoders and gradient CGF features are reliable end-to-end, while the Set Transformer achieves the highest performance with appropriate pretraining. Task-specific pretraining helps when its target captures decision-relevant belief structure, whereas reconstruction pretraining and latent alignment provide more selective benefits. For selecting and training particle-belief encoders in partially observable Markov decision processes, our results show that an encoding that reconstructs the belief well is not necessarily a good input for control.
articles.title_zh: 部分可观察性强化学习的粒子信仰表现

articles.title: From Patterns to Threats: A Deep Learning Model for Anomaly Detection in Cyber-Physical Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cyber-physical systems increasingly rely on interconnected sensing, communication, and control components, creating a need for reliable detection of abnormal behavior. This study proposes a Deep Autoencoder for anomaly detection using the Edge-IIoTset dataset. After preprocessing the full dataset, 2,219,201 observations and 38 numerical features were retained. The proposed model employed a 38-24-12-6-12-24-38 encoder-decoder architecture and was trained exclusively on normal observations to learn representative patterns of expected system behavior. Anomaly decisions were based on reconstruction error, with the classification threshold selected independently from validation data by maximizing the F1-score. To assess model stability, five independent runs were conducted using different random seeds, and results were reported as mean plus or minus standard deviation. The proposed Deep Autoencoder achieved an accuracy of 0.9195 plus or minus 0.0061, precision of 0.9602 plus or minus 0.0204, recall of 0.7348 plus or minus 0.0095, F1-score of 0.8325 plus or minus 0.0121, ROC-AUC of 0.8825 plus or minus 0.0339, and PR-AUC of 0.8640 plus or minus 0.0286. Compared with a Simple Autoencoder baseline, the proposed model improved recall and F1-score while reducing the false positive rate. The results demonstrate that the proposed reconstruction-based representation learning approach can provide an effective and reproducible method for detecting anomalous behavior in cyber-physical environments.
articles.title_zh: 从模式到威胁:网络物理系统异常检测的深层学习模式

articles.title: Reward Blindness: A Theoretical Framework for Diagnosing Reinforcement Learning Reward Limitations in Text-to-SQL
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-SQL systems let users without programming expertise query relational databases in natural language. Reinforcement learning has become the dominant way to train such systems, yet progress is still judged by a single number, execution accuracy, which counts correct queries but says nothing about which kinds of semantic error survive training. This paper develops a theoretical framework that examines text-to-SQL from the perspective of reward design. We introduce Reward Error Sensitivity, a measure of how strongly a reward function separates queries that contain a given error type from queries that do not, and prove a Reward Blindness theorem: when this sensitivity is zero, policy-gradient training carries no systematic signal for removing that error. Using fourteen published finegrained error signals for four text-to-SQL systems on the BIRD benchmark, we build error profiles and estimate sensitivities for common reward designs. Predicate and result-level errors are the most frequent, firing on up to 27 percent of queries, while structurally deep errors such as suboptimal joins persist at 5 to 12 percent. Each reward family has a distinct and predictable set of blind spots, and inexpensive database-level checks that need no language model calls detect 45 to 60 percent of semantic errors. Controlled training simulations confirm that executiononly reward leaves output-preserving errors untouched, whereas a signal-grounded reward removes them even when the detectors are noisy.
articles.title_zh: 奖励失明:在文本到SQL中诊断强化学习奖励限制的理论框架

articles.title: When Learned IDS Model Selection Collapses to a Static Choice: A Measurement Study at the Edge
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Runtime model selection trades detection quality against energy and latency. However, comparing a selector only with a more costly static detector conflates detector choice with the benefit of adaptation. We present a framework for analysis and physical measurement that combines a pairwise reward criterion, matched static controls, paired blocks, a fixed load-prevalence factorial design, and reporting of actions outside training support. On one Raspberry Pi 4B with four frozen TON-IoT detectors, tabular Q-learning and a deep Q-network (DQN) both select LightLR throughout. A retrospective audit using validation data only rules out preference reversals for MedRF versus LightLR and HeavyMLP versus LightLR. However, TinyDT has a higher reward than LightLR in seven of the 2,500 windows, so the audit does not establish global LightLR optimality. We also evaluate a causal DeadlineGuard rule under a fixed factorial design with three arrival rates (50, 100, and 4,000 rows/s) and three attack prevalences (0.10, 0.50, and 0.90). Compared with Static-MedRF, DeadlineGuard saves 43.7 J per 500-s run (2.98%; 95% paired CI 41.4--46.0 J) and eliminates all 512 deadline misses among 5,000 windows, at a cost of 1.373 percentage points in F1. Outside training support, Tabular-Q's deterministic tie-breaking rule selects TinyDT, resulting in a false-positive rate of 67.76%. These single-board results motivate joint audits of reward attainability, realized actions, attribution against matched static controls, service feasibility, and default actions outside training support.
articles.title_zh: 当学会了 IDS 模型选择折叠到静态选择:边缘的测量研究时

articles.title: CARE-3D: Reinforcement Learning for Evidence Grounded Agentic Reasoning in Situated 3D Scenes
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Situated 3D reasoning requires embodied agents to interpret objects, scene geometry, and viewpoint dependent spatial relations. Existing methods learn grounded interactions from supervised traces, but largely imitate prescribed evidence acquisition patterns rather than optimizing the support that the returned evidence provides for the correct answer. Moreover, outcome rewards provide limited credit for intermediate tool choices and may leave infrequent tools underexplored. An effective agent should instead adaptively decide what to ground, which tool to invoke, and how to assess the utility of returned evidence. To this end, this paper presents CARE-3D, a reinforcement post-training framework for adaptive grounded reasoning. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on grounding instructions first establishes valid interactions, after which Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) optimizes the agent while keeping the 3D grounding module frozen. CARE-3D combines Counterfactual Attribution of Returned Evidence for evidence sensitive credit assignment, and Group Coverage Sampling to preserve tool coverage. Experiments on MSQA and Beacon3D show consistent gains over SFT and GRPO using only answer and format rewards, especially in spatial reasoning and grounding answer coherence. Our code is available at \href{https://github.com/xiaoqian-UQ/CARE-3D}{CARE-3D}.
articles.title_zh: CARE-3D:3D场景中基于证据的代理理由强化学习

articles.title: Aligning Judge Models to Be Logically Consistent Multi-Rule Interpreters
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Technical governance of AI models will soon require them to reason over and follow thousands of rules from different jurisdictions. However, as we show in this work, presenting an entire ruleset to a judge model---rather than asking it to judge one rule at a time---changes the way the model interprets the requirements, making it reach conclusions that conflict with its rule-by-rule judgments. We call this challenge multi-rule inconsistency and find that models are more lenient when judging rules embedded within the full ruleset than when judging rules separately. For example, we find that when a safety-critical rule prohibiting a model from pursuing objectives other than those it was given appears in a larger ruleset, all tested judge models are less likely to deem it violated. We examine several methods for reducing inconsistency, including prompting, consistency training using GRPO, and iterative rule refinement. As in human statutory interpretation, surrounding rules shape how a rule is interpreted. Unlike the legal setting, however, these interactions are currently happening implicitly inside the judge model's reasoning. We argue that multi-rule interactions must be measured and handled explicitly by ruleset designers to prevent undetected shifts in interpretation from causing downstream alignment failures.
articles.title_zh: 使法官模型与逻辑一致的多规则口译员保持一致

articles.title: Categorical Foundations of AI Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We follow the idea of separating intelligence from execution and give the categorical foundations of AI agents: the transformers, the agents, and the orchestrations and choreographies of AI agents are categorized, and which also include their coalgebras and algebras.
articles.title_zh: AI代理商的分类基础

articles.title: Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA) for Energy Market Settlements: A Machine and Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.30020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of segmented energy markets into Independent System Operators (ISOs) like CAISO and MISO has increased settlement complexity. Automated transaction processing creates challenges for evaluating accuracy, compliance, and financial integrity. Traditional rule-based manual auditing is inefficient, error-prone, and cannot handle the data volume from automated markets.This research proposes Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA), a machine and reinforcement learning framework for settlement auditing via anomaly prioritization. ANNA integrates statistical anomaly detection, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), clustering, and Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning to flag potentially anomalous transactions from historical market data. The approach is evaluated as an analyst-support tool for prioritizing transactions needing further audit review.ANNA was tested against traditional statistical methods, clustering-based techniques, and supervised/reinforcement learning models. The study used three years of CAISO settlement data over 63 million source records across 32 charge codes and multiple counterparties. After preprocessing, approximately 2.9 million labeled transactions formed the working dataset, with model-specific subsets used for training and evaluation. Performance was assessed using precision, recall, computational efficiency, and false-negative detection.ANNA outperforms traditional methods by identifying hidden relationships in settlement data, while standard deviation thresholds, K-Means, KNN, and Q-Learning performed poorly across key metrics. The result is a scalable solution integrating machine and reinforcement learning for automated auditing of energy market settlements, contributing computationally efficient anomaly prioritization to settlement-auditing workflows.
articles.title_zh: 能源市场结算自动化神经网络审计:基于机器和加强学习的方法

articles.title: SWAM: State-aware World Action Model for Multi-Agent 3D Environments
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.30042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive world models generate virtual environments autoregressively from player actions and visual history. However, visual history alone cannot reliably capture the evolving states of independently acting non-player characters (NPCs) in real games, particularly when they are outside the camera view. Recent multi-agent world models address this challenge through joint multi-view generation or persistent shared state, but often rely on external observations, like maps or scene geometry, or predefined state transitions. We present SWAM, a State-aware World Action Model that separates agent-state evolution from autoregressive visual generation in interactive 3D environments. A lightweight state model propagates character dynamics from actions without consuming generated frames, combining motion priors with learned scene-dependent corrections. The predicted states then guide an autoregressive diffusion transformer alongside visual history through a novel conditioning scheme. Rather than requiring an explicit scene geometry map or visibility tests, the conditioning indicates where characters may appear, allowing the diffusion model to learn their appearance and occlusion. This design enables NPCs to evolve independently of visual generation while maintaining consistent observations across visibility changes, interactions, and respawns. Evaluations in a custom Godot-based first-person shooter game demonstrate improvements in visual fidelity, NPC consistency, and long-horizon stability over existing approaches.
articles.title_zh: SWAM: 具有国家意识的多智能体3D环境世界行动模式

articles.title: EVD-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for EEG-to-Image Decoding
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.30061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: EEG-to-image decoding recovers visual information from non-invasive brain recordings, providing a window into human perception. However, comparisons across systems are confounded by a variable that is rarely reported as such: which participants' data the system was allowed to use. The same Top-1 score on a 200-way gallery may come from a per-participant system, a pooled model over all participants, or a model that never saw the test participant---cases that differ by more than most architectural changes between the methods being compared. We present \bench, a benchmark on THINGS-EEG2 that standardizes the gallery and EEG input, matches training budgets across systems within each regime, and compares three participant-access regimes: within-subject, joint-subject, and strict leave-one-subject-out, with unlabeled target calibration reported separately. All three settings evaluate concept-level zero-shot retrieval: the 200 test concepts are disjoint from the 1,654 concepts used for EEG--image fitting and validation. We compare retrieval across access regimes and use zero-EEG and matched-wrong EEG controls to assess dependence on correct EEG--stimulus pairing. We vary trial averaging, gallery size and difficulty, and training data coverage, and compare target adaptation and visual feature targets. We also assess sensitivity to EEG window length and channel count, robustness to input perturbations, and confidence calibration. These results establish participant-access regime as a necessary reporting dimension alongside gallery, repetition, and visual target.
articles.title_zh: EVD- Bench: EEG对图像解码的综合基准

articles.title: Post-Training Agents for Long-Document Reasoning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.30090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Professional documents are a long-context workload that retrieval-style benchmarks do not capture. In a ten-domain enterprise collection, a task's evidence is spread across a source document of median length 27 pages (mean 48.8, maximum 873); a third of tasks rest mainly on charts, drawings, and maps; and 70.9% require two or more reasoning hops. We post-train Kimi-K2.7, an open-weight foundation model, at its full context window on 1,465 expert-authored tasks with atomic rubrics from that collection, training rank-32 adapters with one round of privileged-context on-policy self-distillation followed by two rounds of rubric-reward reinforcement learning. We render each PDF as text for training and as extracted text plus selected page images at evaluation.
